mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown consistent week-on-week improvement from -12.4% to -9.7% over the past three weeks, indicating a steady recovery trend independent of external shocks. This momentum will persist over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC further toward baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 2.7 percentage points over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or reverses by more than 2 percentage points in any single week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility remains severely depressed at -30.6%, constraining commuter access to retail districts. If TRANSIT fails to recover above -25% within two weeks, retail foot traffic will remain suppressed as consumers cannot reach shopping venues efficiently.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -25% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -30.6% in t-0w, showing minimal recovery
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers to -20% or higher within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases despite TRANSIT remaining below -25%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has stabilized around -20% after sharp decline from -34.7%, indicating outdoor recreation substitution is reaching saturation. As outdoor venues reach capacity constraints, consumers will redirect discretionary spending to indoor retail venues, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stabilizes within 2 percentage points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -34.7% to -21.4% then stabilized
failure_condition: PARKS continues to decline or RETAIL_REC does not increase when PARKS stabilization occurs, indicating no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-August in Sydney marks the onset of spring school holidays and early spring shopping season. GROCERY_PHARM stability at +1.7% reflects maintained essential mobility, which will extend to discretionary retail as seasonal demand accelerates, driving RETAIL_REC positive over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining elevated, or GROCERY_PHARM declines below +1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized at -10.9% to -12.1%, indicating remote work adoption is entrenched. This persistent workplace absence reduces weekday commuter retail traffic. Combined with TRANSIT depression at -30.6%, the dual suppression will keep RETAIL_REC below baseline over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains between -10% and -13% AND TRANSIT remains below -28%
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES recovers above -8% or TRANSIT recovers above -25%, or RETAIL_REC increases despite both conditions holding.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has plateaued at +5.3% to +6.7%, indicating sustained stay-at-home behavior from policy or behavioral adaptation. Elevated residential presence suppresses retail mobility as consumers remain home-based. This regime will persist, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +5.0% for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL elevated at +5.3% to +6.7% across all four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL drops below +3.0% or RETAIL_REC increases above -5% despite RESIDENTIAL remaining elevated.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES recovery from -12.1% to -10.9% signals gradual return-to-office momentum. If this trend accelerates to -8% or better within one week, commuter foot traffic will increase, triggering retail recovery as office workers resume shopping during commute windows, lifting RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by more than 1.5 percentage points in a single week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 1.2 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES does not improve by 1.5+ points in the next week, or RETAIL_REC does not respond within two weeks of such improvement.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS decline from -34.7% to -21.4% combined with TRANSIT depression at -30.6% indicates consumers are neither using outdoor recreation nor public transport. This dual constraint forces substitution toward private vehicle-based retail access. If TRANSIT remains below -28% while PARKS stabilizes, private retail mobility will increase, lifting RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stabilizes within 2 points AND TRANSIT remains below -28%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks when both conditions are met, or TRANSIT recovers above -25% before RETAIL_REC responds.
